page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not feature any local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core processing metrics from stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 25% tier, with single-threaded gzip compression falling into the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by Passmark CPU and Geekbench multi-core evaluations. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for large blocks also perform at average levels, although the overall Passmark memory score remains in the lower 25% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.4xlarge offers a dense memory allocation relative to its processing cores, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute power. The instance is best suited for applications such as caching layers, Redis deployments, database operations, and multi-threaded text or image processing tasks.
